label: At GO, low after a rewarded S1 trial and high after reaching S2.
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S2) * ep_trial
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 8 is near saturation at D1/D2 and falls across the episode at GO (timing R^2 0.83). Beyond timing, the GO value depends mostly on the last trial: strongly lowered after a rewarded S1 trial (a1 S1 r -0.46, a2 S1 r -0.27), raised after reaching S2 (rewarded or not, +0.1 to +0.4), so it acts as a last-outcome S1-vs-S2 signal where S1-rewarded pushes it negative. At D1 an unrewarded previous trial lowers it, more so later in the episode (and more after S1 unrewarded or consecutive losses). A small graded negative belief_lo effect at GO/D2 adds little. The free fit adds only ~0.06 R^2 over the short form (short is ~89% of free fit), and both are below the all-observed table ceiling (0.67), so some last-trial x choice structure is still missing.

issues: The label leaves out the third short-form term, (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_trial. That term adds about 0.077 test R^2 beyond timing (0.397 without it, 0.474 with it), so a reader of the label alone would not predict the D1 drop after unrewarded trials late in the episode.

'Raised after reaching S2, whether rewarded or not' is only partly right. The GO residuals after S2 are a1 S2 r +0.33, a1 S2 u +0.40, a2 S2 r +0.11 and a2 S2 u +0.34, so a2 S2 r is weak. a2 S1 u also gives +0.23 without reaching S2. Misses on the recorded form show systematic under-prediction at GO after a2 S1 u (+0.20), a1 S2 u (+0.17) and a2 S1 r (+0.16), and over-prediction at GO after a2 S2 r (-0.11).

Replacing GO*(prev_state==S2) with GO*(prev_reward==0) scores better on test: 0.490 vs 0.474 (dev 0.495). So the raising factor is better described as 'the previous trial was unrewarded' than 'the previous trial reached S2'.

The D1 effect is really about losing at S1. The D1 residuals are a1 S1 u -0.23 and a2 S1 u -0.31, against -0.02 and -0.05 after an S2 loss. Misses show D1 after a2 S1 u over-predicted by 0.17. The explanation mentions this, but the short form's 'unrewarded' term merges both states.

Systematic cell errors of 0.2-0.3 at GO remain in both forms (the revised form misses GO after a1 S2 r by +0.30 and after a1 S1 u by -0.25). The last-trial table alone reaches 0.58 and all observed variables reach 0.67, so the 3-term short form misses some choice x state x reward structure. Still, the main effect (the dip at GO after a rewarded S1 trial, weight -0.46) holds up and the short form meets the explained threshold.
The belief_lo terms add almost nothing: GO*belief_lo in place of the D1 term scores 0.398. This is consistent with the explanation's claim that belief adds little.
